title: Microsoft Teams: allowed list of external meeting notetaker bots
summary: The briefing passes: the planned allow list is clearly distinguished from today's bot-detection policy, and its roadmap details match the record. Microsoft Learn supports the existing control, approval and blocking behaviour, recovery qualifications and Teams licensing requirement; searches found no documented configuration or default for the planned list.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to let admins configure an allowed list of external meeting notetaker bots.
claims.quote: Admins will be able to configure a list of external meeting bots which are allowed to join meetings hosted in their organization.

claims.claim: The planned control governs meetings hosted in the organisation, not meetings its users attend elsewhere.
claims.quote: Admins will be able to configure more granular and advanced controls for managing external bots and their access to meetings hosted in their organization.

claims.where: controls[0]; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: An admin UI or API for the planned allowed-bots list is not yet documented in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams allowed external meeting bot list configuration policy scope assignment admin center; "Teams" "allowed" "bots" "PowerShell". Opened Manage external bots and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; neither documents a named allow list.

claims.claim: The existing control is in Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting Join and Lobby > Manage external bots and their access to meetings.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Meetings > Meeting policies. Select the policy you want to modify, or create a new policy. Under Meeting join & lobby, find Manage external bots and their access to meetings.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalBotAccessMode RequireApprovalWhenDetected sets the existing policy to require approval for detected bots.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy
    [[-Identity] <XdsIdentity>]
[-ExternalBotAccessMode <String>]
RequireApprovalWhenDetected: When detected, bots will be enforced to the meeting lobby, regardless of the lobby setting of the meeting. They will require approval before getting access to the meetings.

claims.claim: Teams uses signals collected during the meeting join process to detect external bots.

claims.claim: Under When detected, require approval before joining, detected bots enter the lobby regardless of its configuration.
claims.quote: When detected, require approval before joining: Detected bots are placed in the meeting lobby regardless of the meeting's lobby configuration.

claims.claim: Detected bots require explicit admission under the approval option.
claims.quote: Organizers (also presenters, depending on the meeting setting), need to explicitly admit these bots into the meeting.

claims.claim: The Teams Bot Identification Program is a public preview for independent software vendors building Teams meeting bots.
claims.quote:
Microsoft Teams Bot Identification Program (Public Preview)
Microsoft is also introducing the Teams Bot Identification Program to support independent software vendors (ISVs) that build meeting bot experiences for Teams.

claims.claim: Eligible bot providers can register with Microsoft through the program.
claims.quote: Through this program, eligible bot providers can register with Microsoft and include a self-identification marker in their meeting join requests.

claims.claim: Learn does not document the relationship between the Bot Identification Program and the planned allow list.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams allowed list external meeting notetaker bots licensing pricing recovery identification Bot Identification Program 580451. Read Teams Bot Identification Program and Manage external bots; they link registration to detection, not to a named allowed-bots list.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes entry control without giving bots access beyond that of a regular external participant.
claims.quote: The allowed bots will be treated like a regular external participant to the meeting and meeting policies will be enforced as appropriate.

claims.claim: Detection can incorrectly identify a human participant as a bot.
claims.quote: Incorrect bot detection: Detection may incorrectly identify a human participant as a bot.

claims.claim: Under Require approval before joining, organisers can admit a misclassified participant from the lobby.
claims.quote: Require approval before joining: Organizers can admit the participant from the lobby and use the This is not a bot option to correct the participant's representation in that meeting.

claims.claim: Under the approval option, organisers can mark a misclassified person using This is not a bot.
claims.quote: Require approval before joining: Organizers can admit the participant from the lobby and use the This is not a bot option to correct the participant's representation in that meeting.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Under Block all detected bots, detected participants are blocked rather than placed in the lobby.
claims.quote: Block all detected bots: Detected bots are automatically blocked from joining the meeting. They aren't placed in the meeting lobby for organizer approval, and meeting organizers can't admit them.

claims.claim: Organisers cannot admit participants blocked by the existing Block all detected bots option.
claims.quote: They aren't placed in the meeting lobby for organizer approval, and meeting organizers can't admit them.

claims.claim: Where supported, eligible people incorrectly identified as bots can use email verification recovery to verify their identity and attempt to join.
claims.quote: Block all detected bots: Participants incorrectly identified as bots may be prevented from joining the meeting. Where supported, eligible participants can use the email verification recovery experience to verify their identity and attempt to join.

claims.claim: Recovery for the planned allowed-bots list is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams allowed external meeting bot list identification matching vendor domain high friction lobby transcript storage recovery. Read Manage external bots and Teams Bot Identification Program; recovery is documented for existing detection settings, not the planned list.

claims.claim: The existing external-bots setting is a meeting policy applied at user or group level.
claims.quote:
Scope: Meetings policies at a user / group level
The setting applies to meetings hosted by users assigned the meeting policy.

claims.claim: The existing control can be configured tenant-wide in the default org-wide policy or for specific users or groups through targeted policies.
claims.quote: Configure this meeting policy at the tenant level with the default org-wide meeting policy or configure for a specific user group/user by creating or modifying the appropriate targeted meeting policy.

claims.claim: The external-bots guide marks its content as applying to meetings, not events.
